name: Verb
a: An instruction: one step that the processor does, for example MOV or ADD.
b: A statement that does something, for example PRINT, CALL or ALLOCATE.

name: Noun
a: A register, a flag, a port or a place in memory, for example AX.
b: A kind of value (a type), for example INTEGER or REAL.

name: Adjective
idea: A word that describes a noun.
a: A size word, for example BYTE (8 bits) or WORD (16 bits).
b: An attribute, for example ALLOCATABLE or PARAMETER.

name: Adverb
idea: A word that changes how a verb acts.
a: A prefix, for example REP: do the next verb again, CX times.
b: A word that changes a loop, for example CONCURRENT in DO CONCURRENT.

name: Idiom
idea: A ready-made phrase with a fixed meaning.
a: A BIOS or DOS service call, for example INT 21h with AH=09h: show a line of text.
b: A built-in function or subroutine, for example SQRT or MATMUL.

name: Grammar mark
idea: Punctuation and signs that join words into a sentence.
a: Commas between operands, [square brackets] for memory, a colon after a label.
b: Maths signs (+ - * / **), the = sign, and (:) for part of an array.

name: Note to the translator
idea: A word for the translator only. The processor never sees it.
a: An assembler directive, for example ORG, DB or %macro.
b: A structure word, for example PROGRAM, MODULE or CONTAINS.
